title: Tetris: A Compilation Framework for VQA Applications in Quantum Computing
problem: Near-term quantum computers running variational quantum algorithms suffer from high error rates and execution time costs due to two-qubit gates, which are an order of magnitude more expensive than single-qubit gates. Existing VQA compilers miss optimization opportunities during circuit synthesis.
motivation: Efficient compilation of VQA applications is essential for practical execution on near-term quantum devices with limited qubit counts and shallow circuit depths.
method: Tetris exploits previously overlooked circuit synthesis opportunities to reduce two-qubit gate counts. It uses a refined intermediate representation based on Pauli strings to identify two-qubit gate elimination opportunities. The framework includes a fast bridging approach to mitigate hardware mapping costs when placing gates on physical qubits.
key_novelty: Using a Pauli string intermediate representation to reveal and exploit two-qubit gate reduction opportunities in the circuit synthesis stage that state-of-the-art compilers miss.
contributions: 41.3% reduction in CNOT gate counts through circuit synthesis optimization
37.9% reduction in circuit depth compared to state-of-the-art approaches
Pauli string IR enabling identification of redundant two-qubit gates
Fast bridging approach for efficient hardware mapping with reduced placement overhead
